name: Hangable Auto Bulb
editorial_article: 'Hangable Auto Bulb' stands as a landmark release in the evolution of electronic music, capturing Richard D. James—under his AFX moniker—during a highly experimental period in 1995. Originally issued as two distinct 12-inch EPs, this project signaled a radical departure from the moody, analogue-heavy textures of his earlier works, such as '...I Care Because You Do'. Instead, James turned his attention to the burgeoning drum and bass scene, specifically the work of Cornish producer Luke Vibert (Plug). The resulting sound, characterized by hyper-accelerated, computer-arranged breakbeats, timestretched samples, and intricate percussive patterns, effectively codified the 'drill 'n' bass' subgenre. \n\nBeyond its technical innovations, the project is notable for its playful and enigmatic approach to titling and production. The title itself is an anagram of 'Analogue Bubblebath', referencing his earlier EP series, and several tracks feature complex anagrams for titles, including 'Laughable Butane Bob' and 'Arched Maid Via RDJ' (a reference to his own name). Sonically, the project oscillates between jarring, volatile rhythm programming and delicate, ethereal melodies, a dichotomy that would become a hallmark of the Aphex Twin style. Decades later, 'Hangable Auto Bulb' remains a vital, alien-sounding document that redefined what was possible with electronic rhythmic arrangement, influencing an entire generation of producers. By blending these fractured, restless beats with a subtle, melodic warmth, James created a blueprint for IDM and experimental electronics that continues to sound fresh and technically daring to modern ears.

editorial_pitch: Released in 1995 as two separate EPs and later compiled, 'Hangable Auto Bulb' captures Richard D. James at a pivotal turning point, pioneering the hyper-kinetic, glitch-heavy sound that would become known as drill 'n' bass. It remains a masterclass in the tension between complex, fractured rhythms and the haunting, beautiful melodic sensibilities that define his work.
